You can white-label Cal.com to be a scheduling feature baked right inside of your own product, or interact with it via their API directly or any of the best automation tools on the market. ### Open Source

Unlike most of the meeting scheduler options on the market, Cal is open source, meaning it's free to self-host, and you can view all of their code on GitHub.

## Pricing

Cal.com has different pricing options for those who want to white-label/build with Cal (head over to their website to see those).

## Final Verdict

So is Cal.com worth it? If you are looking for a new scheduler that is flexible, then yes absolutely it is. [...] ### Scheduler

The main feature of Cal is being able to easily schedule meetings with others, that said, it's only just scratching the surface into everything it can do. When we say that Cal.com can cover all your scheduling needs, we mean it 😄

Yes! You can take payments with Cal.com. It integrates with payment processors like Stripe so you can collect payment during the booking process.

While you can still use Google Meet or Zoom with Cal, they also have their own baked in video meeting software that is pretty slick, although we still prefer to use Google Meet with Granola AI for our calls.

results.content:
### Where Cal.com Shines

 Free plan depth. Unlimited event types, payments and CRM sync for one user at $0.
 Developer tooling. API v2, Atoms and a Platform plan for embedding scheduling.
 Team routing. Weighted round robin and routing forms with CRM ownership rules.
 Built-in video. Cal Video with recording and transcription on every plan.
 Compliance paperwork. SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 reports downloadable inside the app.

### Where Cal.com Falls Short [...] ## What Is Cal.com?

Cal.com is a scheduling platform for individuals, teams and developers who build booking into their own products. You connect Google, Outlook, Apple or Zoho calendars, publish booking links, and let people pick a slot. On top of that sit round-robin and collective events for teams, routing forms, workflows for email and SMS reminders, a built-in video tool, payments and an AI phone agent. The developer side includes API v2, Atoms (React components) and a Platform plan for SaaS companies that embed scheduling. Since April 2026 it is a closed-source product run by Cal.com, Inc.

## Who Is Cal.com Best For?

Cal.com fits people who want many event types for free, or who need scheduling that plugs into a CRM or their own code. [...] > Verdict. Cal.com is still a capable scheduler with a free plan that includes unlimited event types, Stripe and PayPal payments, and two-way Salesforce and HubSpot sync for a single user.  
> What changed. Cal.com moved its production code to a private repository in April 2026, so the open-source argument most reviews still repeat no longer applies to the hosted product.  
> The deadline. Cal.eu, the EU-hosted region, shuts down on 1 November 2026, and its users are being moved to the US company's international platform.  
> Who should look elsewhere. EU teams that chose Cal.com for data residency or for self-hosting with team features now need a different plan.

results.title: Cal.com review | Fabric – The workspace that thinks with you
results.content:
The product covers the same core workflow as Calendly, SavvyCal, or Acuity Scheduling: you define event types with durations, availability windows, and meeting locations, then distribute links via email signatures, websites, or direct messages. Where Cal.com diverges is in the philosophy underneath. The codebase is public, the API is central to the product rather than an afterthought, and the architecture is built to be embedded inside other applications rather than standing alone.

Video conferencing is supported through integrations with Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams, as well as Cal Video, the platform's own built-in video tool powered by Daily.co. Cal Video is included free, which means you can offer video meetings without subscribing to a separate conferencing service. [...] What is Cal AI?

Cal AI is Cal.com's AI-powered scheduling assistant. It can handle booking requests via natural language, acting as an automated coordinator that understands scheduling intent and manages the back-and-forth of finding mutual availability. It is designed to work alongside the standard booking page flow for situations where conversational scheduling is more appropriate.

Is Fabric free?

Fabric has a free tier that lets you get started at no cost. Paid plans are available at $8 per month with annual billing or $10 per month billed monthly. Fabric plants trees for every paid subscriber. You can learn more about the environmental commitment on the environment page. [...] ### Free tier

The free plan costs nothing and has no time limit. It includes one user, unlimited event types, unlimited calendar connections, email and SMS notifications, Cal Video, Stripe and PayPal payments, two-way Salesforce and HubSpot sync, and access to over 100 app integrations. You also get a one-click Calendly import tool that migrates your event types and settings.

This is one of the most generous free tiers in the scheduling space. Calendly's free plan limits you to a single event type, which makes it difficult to use for anything beyond the simplest scheduling needs. Cal.com imposes no such restriction, which means individuals can run a complete scheduling setup without paying anything.
